title: Research exact p=25 root-pair decoder boundary
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds `research/p25-root-pair-bound-seed632639/`, a scoped exact obstruction for eight-term, all-pairs decoders whose row and column normals are E8 roots, at exactly 25 punctures. Each root support has 63 distinct extremal 25-line masks that first lower its live label span to dimension seven. Across the 120 root directions, all 7,560 masks are distinct, so one puncture set can lower at most one root-normal support.

The rank inequality `rank(X,Y) >= dim(X)+dim(Y)-9` then gives a total separate COPY bill of at least 54: at most one term can use the exceptional support, costing at least five even when the same root appears on both sides of that term; the other seven terms cost at least seven each. This is a new p=25 boundary result beyond the p<=24 floor. It is not a decoder supplier or a new exponent.

At 95 live ports, the best compatible center profile `(5,7,7,7,7,7,7,7)` has exact pinned ceiling interval `[0.001538546310035, 0.001538546310036]`, 8.965% below the selected local-word ceiling. Added setup, frames, transitions, hosting, precision and restoration are all set to zero. The result closes this root-pair route against the 5% task gate under the unchanged coverage law; arbitrary dual bases, masked identities and nine or more terms remain outside scope.

## Task and overlap

- Exact base: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`.
- Track/card: `complex-mechanisms / complex-rank-shape-decoder`; seed `632639f1d387026a8b953fa82c286d82`; selector scope key `02b31ebd160542c86299`; priority revision 4; catalogue SHA-256 `d46eb6d5b3e279428753d770653663fbdf1063e55c255ea073d768f344927ef7`.
- Selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`; certificate SHA-256 `1122cb3a575f8c788345fc1bf4c108ac7c3250fb81a5988671f5eb04b3ab3045`.
- Scope status: **changed** from block-frame climbs to the exact p=25 support boundary in the root-pair dual-basis family. The new parameter boundary is the first one beyond the p<=24 theorem and directly tests whether lower copy rank can change the paid local profile.
- Predecessors: [PR #717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717), [PR #968](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968), [PR #1619](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1619), and [PR #1624](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1624). PR #1624 treats one fixed p=26 object; this package covers all p=25 masks for the root-pair family.
- Active neighboring work checked: [Discussion #1622](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1622) studies ten-term P112 gauges; [Discussion #1952](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1952) studies cyclic masked rank-three profiles; [Discussion #2119](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2119) studies rank-six phase schedules. Open [PR #2232](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2232), head `3391f27dd0f226f0e1ead8b2b829eb6d3ec567d3`, screens four-term E6 projected-Gram decoders with an adapted pairing; its 36 E6 lines and projection model differ from this E8 p=25 family. Open [PR #2228](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2228), head `ad1757e319225f3a5b86e3d3fa72897bd9f6db40`, provides a broader dense root-code floor and lists E8, P112 and P104 cases. This package supplies the exact p=25 extremal-mask census and an eight-term dual-root bound; it does not claim to exceed that broader theorem.
- Claim and result: [Discussion #1167 comment 18937692](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-18937692).

## Validation

Reproduce from repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/p25-root-pair-bound-seed632639/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/p25-root-pair-bound-seed632639/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p25-root-pair-bound-seed632639 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p25-root-pair-bound-seed632639
```

Both exact verifier modes pass under CPython 3.14.7; the metadata and source-pin check passes. The registered replay could not run locally because Python 3.12 is not installed; GitHub CI will run the declared Python 3.12 commands. The source manifest pins the base, task catalogue, selected result, review, source manifest, certificate, predecessor model, and ceiling engine. The selected record's reproduction command remains `make frontier1094-verify`; it was not rerun because this PR does not modify that source chain.

The finite checker reconstructs the 120 root lines and rank-nine label pairing, tests all 130,305 functional pairs for every root support, verifies 7,560 distinct extremal masks and their exact residual ranks, checks the 24-puncture and second-root controls, and recomputes the rational ceiling. The written argument in the README derives the decoder COPY floor from the exact support census and the binary rank inequality. This is not a formal proof of the full multiplication theorem.

## Credit

Retains the PR717/PR968 E8 model and p<=24 theorem, PR1619's favorable port/copy price, the selected #1094 source chain, and PR1624's distinct fixed p=26 work. All are pinned in `SOURCES.json` and the task card. New work is Apache-2.0. Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scope selection, exact enumeration, proof development, pricing, verifier implementation and writing; no independent human or proof-assistant review is claimed.

## Open next questions

Can a non-root dual basis or an overcomplete/masked decoder at p=25 avoid the one-exceptional-root restriction and pass the fully charged local moment gate? The root-pair result does not cover those alphabets. The smallest next step is to choose one explicit non-root support alphabet, derive its exact support-rank floor and screen the complete local profile before synthesis. A source-aligned frame and full setup/hosting/precision/restoration invoice are currently missing.
